faq_a1: No. TalentRadar runs next to it and nothing moves. A list of companies from your CRM or a spreadsheet is enough. You download the new roles as a file to import into Bullhorn or Vincere, or as a generic CSV. There’s no direct connection to a specific ATS yet; you download the new roles as a file, or we send them over the API and webhooks.
faq_a2: Not at all. Watching companies and roles needs no ATS. If you want one, every plan includes Radar + ATS: candidates, contacts, jobs, pipeline and placements. It’s deliberately simple, built for small agencies.
faq_a3: It reads roles from Jobs.cz and Teamio, from company ATS (Greenhouse, Lever, Workable, Ashby, SmartRecruiters, Workday, Personio, BambooHR, Teamtailor, Recruitee, Pinpoint, HireHive, Phenom, Jibe, SuccessFactors, Oracle Recruiting, Eightfold) and from ordinary career pages. Out of it you get Excel, a generic CSV and an import file for Bullhorn and Vincere. You can also take the data over the API and webhooks (Agency Pro and Scale). We connect unusual career sites to order on the Scale plan.
faq_a4: When the ad disappears from the site, the next scan notices, the one after confirms it, and TalentRadar archives the role. A careers page that’s briefly down won’t wipe your list. If the company posts the role again, it comes back with its history and notes.
faq_a5: The trial lasts 14 days, with no credit card, the features of Agency Pro and up to 150 companies. Within 48 hours of sending your list it’s fully working; companies whose career page can’t be found automatically, I look up by hand. Three days before the end I’ll get in touch. If you want to carry on, you pick a plan and I send you an invoice. The trial never turns into a paid plan by itself.
faq_a6: No. When you search for a candidate you only paste the profile, and once you’ve searched it’s gone. Before anything goes to the AI (Google’s Gemini via its paid API, which doesn’t use the data for training) we take out the name, e-mail, phone and links. Candidates are stored only if you add them yourself in Radar + ATS.
faq_a7_html: TalentRadar is run by its founder, Kryštof Pejša, who is also the controller of personal data. Every agency has its own separate database and sees only its own data. The app and its database run in the EU, the server in the Netherlands and the database in Ireland. Who helps us run the website and the app, what goes to the AI and how long we keep the data is set out in our privacy policy.
faq_a10: Exporting your companies and roles works at any time, so you always have your data. If TalentRadar were to close, I would announce it at least 3 months ahead and refund any prepaid months.
faq_a9: You can download your companies and roles to Excel or CSV at any time, or as a file for Bullhorn or Vincere. If you don’t continue after the trial, I stop the account and you pay nothing. I delete the agency’s data within 90 days of the end of the trial or subscription, or sooner on request.
faq_a8: We read only pages that companies publish for job seekers themselves, and public ATS APIs. We don’t read LinkedIn: you open the search link yourself.

how_ch0_body: You see where a role in your field has opened since yesterday, at clients and at the companies you want to win, each on its own. One click narrows the list to roles open for 45 days or more: there the company most likely isn’t filling it on its own.
how_ch0_body_m: You see where a role in your field has opened since yesterday, at clients and at the companies you want to win, each on its own. One click narrows the list to roles open for 45 days or more: there the company most likely isn’t filling it on its own.
how_ch2_body: Every role comes with a reason to get in touch: a fresh role, a role open for 45 days or more, or a company you haven’t dealt with in a while. From the role’s title we estimate who most likely decides on the hire, and one click looks for them on LinkedIn. The draft message is in your own style, and you send it yourself.

story_body_html: In Dublin I worked at the recruitment agency Ingenio Global, run by Rob Magee. Every Monday, experienced headhunters there went through clients’ career pages and copied links into spreadsheets. I wrote a system that does it by itself, and it watched 180 companies there for two months. Today it is TalentRadar. I’m eighteen and I build it on my own; that’s why you can export at any time, cancel monthly, and I would announce an end three months ahead.

trial_ai_brief:
Prepare a company list for TalentRadar, a service that tracks where companies are hiring.

Source: [attach a CRM export or your client list, or describe the sectors and region we care about]

Return only the table as plain text, with no introduction, no comment and no code block. At most 150 rows. The separator is a semicolon. The first row must be exactly:
Company;Careers page;Last contact;Had placement

Rules:
- Company: the company name, each company only once.
- Careers page: the address of the page with open roles, or at least the company website, only if you are sure of it. Don't make addresses up.
- Last contact: the date of the last contact with the company as 15/03/2024, only if it is in the source. Otherwise empty.
- Had placement: yes or no, only if the source says so. Otherwise empty.
- Do not include people's names, emails, phone numbers or candidates.

Example:
Company;Careers page;Last contact;Had placement
Air Bank;airbank.cz/careers;15/03/2024;yes
Rohlik Group;rohlik.cz;;
